claims.explanation: AZD7762 is a CHK1/CHK2 inhibitor that selectively kills tumor cells with a defective G1 DNA-damage checkpoint, forcing reliance on CHK1-dependent G2 arrest and homologous recombination repair; TP53 mutation (and other G1 checkpoint lesions) therefore sensitizes, while intact p53 or intact HR protects. The pattern is further shaped by replication stress and DNA-repair proficiency, so oncogene-driven, HR-deficient, or replication-stressed lines are more sensitive.

features.basis: Loss of G1 checkpoint creates dependence on CHK1-mediated G2 arrest; p53-mutant lines are preferentially radiosensitized by AZD7762 (PMID 20233881, 22446188)
Higher CHK1 expression/activity maintains the G2 checkpoint and DNA repair, reducing sensitivity to CHK1 inhibition (PMID 18790776, 22117197)
AZD7762 inhibits homologous recombination and Rad51 focus formation; intact HR capacity protects cells (PMID 20501833)
ATM loss impairs DNA damage signaling and repair, increasing reliance on CHK1 and sensitivity to checkpoint inhibition (PMID 20501833)
HR deficiency from BRCA1 loss mimics the HR impairment caused by CHK1 inhibition, increasing sensitivity
HR deficiency from BRCA2 loss mimics the HR impairment caused by CHK1 inhibition, increasing sensitivity
Cyclin E overexpression causes replication stress and dependence on CHK1 for survival
MYC-driven replication stress increases reliance on CHK1; virtual cell shows MYC downregulation after AZD7762
KRAS-mutant tumors show increased replication stress and DNA damage, sensitizing to checkpoint inhibition
PTEN loss impairs DNA repair and increases genomic instability, sensitizing to CHK1 inhibition
CDKN2A loss compromises G1 checkpoint control, increasing dependence on CHK1
RB1 loss dysregulates G1/S transition and increases reliance on G2 checkpoint
